subject: Specifying t-distributions on measurement part of SEM

messages.author: f911fee5a7d9903f
messages.subject: Specifying t-distributions on measurement part of SEM
parts:
Hello,

I am new to blavaan and to bayesian SEM. I am trying to specify t-distributions on the below "measurement part" of my SEM:

semmodel <- ' 

# Measurement Part
workshop =~ zeroneg+dialogqual+checkin+pgrpnumber

# Regressions
DAS_gain ~ A*workshop + B*FAD_gain + C*PSS_gain + CC*Trait_gain
workshop ~ D*white + E*gender + G*jobstress + H*tools
FAD_gain ~ I*gender + J*white + K*jobstress + L*PSS_gain + M*Trait_gain
PSS_gain ~ N*white + O*gender + P*jobstress + Q*Trait_gain
tools ~ R*white + S*gender + T*jobstress
Trait_gain ~ U*white + V*gender + W*jobstress + X*tools + Y*workshop

'

# Unique priors for mv intercepts; parallel chains
fit <- bsem(semmodel, data=dat2,
            dp=dpriors(nu="dnorm(5,1e-2)"),
            bcontrol=list(method="rjparallel"))
summary(fit)

I have read the blavaan article on exporting into jags, but have not been successful at running both the measurement and regression syntax. 

Is there a way to specify t-distributions all in rjags without using blavaan? I'm also curious why using the "=~" measurement syntax doesn't work in the below. 

Here is what I currently have (curtailed in some redundant places to save space):

modelstring = "

model {
for (i in 1:nData)
{

##Distribution for the outcome (DAS_gain; changes in relationship satisfaction) 
DAS_gain[i]~dnorm(mu1[i],tau1)

##Model for DAS_gain
mu1[i]<-a0 + a1*workshop[i] + a2*FAD_gain[i]+ a3*PSS_gain[i] + a4*Trait_gain

##Distrubution and model for Workshop 
workshop[i]~dnorm(mu2[i], tau2)
mu2[i]<-b0 + b1*white[i] + b2*gender[i] + b3*jobstress[i] + b4*tools[i]

##Distribution and model for FAD_gain
FAD_gain[i]~dnorm(mu3[i], tau3)
mu3[i]<-c0 + c1*gender[i] + c2*white[i] + c3*jobstress[i] + c4*PSS_gain[i] + c5*Trait_gain[i]

##Distribution and model for PSS_gain
PSS_gain[i]~dnorm(mu4[i], tau4)
mu4[i]<-d0 + d1*white[i] + d2*gender[i] + d3*jobstress[i] + d4*Trait_gain[i] 
 
           ...and so on
 
}

#--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Priors on regression coefficients - normal weakly informative
a0 ~ dnorm(200,.01)
a1 ~ dnorm(5,.01)
a2 ~ dnorm(5,.01)
a3 ~ dnorm(5,.01)
a4 ~ dnorm(5,.01)
b0 ~ dnorm(5,.01)
b1 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
b2 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
b3 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
b4 ~ dnorm(1,.01) 
c0 ~ dnorm(5,.01)
c1 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
c2 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
c3 ~ dnorm(1,.01)
           ...and so on

# Priors on Precisions - gamma non-informative
tau1 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
tau2 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
tau3 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
tau4 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
tau5 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
tau6 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
tau7 ~ dgamma(0.01,0.01)
           ...and so on 

}
"
```

Any advice is appreciated! Thank you.
Bayesian Structural Equation Models - arXiv

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Specifying t-distributions on measurement part of SEM
parts:
Travis,

I assume that you saw around Fig 4 of the blavaan paper, which shows
how to insert t distributions in the jags code? If not, that section
hopefully provides some help.

I don't immediately see problems with the code that you posted, but it
is also hard to say without a full example. I would first try running
your desired model (except without t distributions) using the bsem
command, to make sure that works. Then export the jags syntax from
that working model, then edit in the t distributions.

Would also be good to make sure you have the latest blavaan version on
CRAN (0.3-3), which contains some bug fixes.

Best,
Ed
